title: Say why a plan failed and why a project waits

blocks.text: Problem statement
Two messages arrived the same week. From finance, after trying a budget cut:
We cut 2030 and 2031 to $4M each and the planner just said "infeasible". Infeasible why? Which of our numbers is the problem?
And from a regional manager:
P030 is our biggest Valley project and it's not funded. Why not? What would it take?

You start from the planner of the lesson before, whose rows all carry names. When a request has no plan, name exactly the rules that clash, in the planners' words, so that dropping or changing any one of them gives a plan; a rule that plays no part in the clash is not named. When a project is left out, say what funding it would cost (the NPV given up and the projects dropped) or, when no plan can fund it, which rules block it. The command line explains an infeasible request, and `--why PROJECT` explains a project the plan leaves out.
`--why` for a project the plan funds prints nothing after the report; for an infeasible request the command line prints the conflict, does not answer `--why`, and returns 1.

Run's report gains a section: `main.py` now asks why P003 was left out of the demo plan, as `--why P003` does. After the report it prints `P003 cannot be funded. ` and the conflict message on the same line; the message's first line is `No plan meets these <n> rules together; drop or change any one of them:` and each next line is `  <row>: <description>` (two spaces first), one per row of the conflict in name order. The frontier section of the lesson before follows, unchanged.

`cipt/scenario.py` and `cipt/store.py` are the next lesson's stubs, as the reference has them; no code of this step imports them, so leave them as they are. Submit runs every test in `tests/`, the earlier steps' included, and compares Run's report with the expected one.
Blueprint
Write each method below. The tests check each one by itself and the whole program end to end, so you may change any other part of the code as you see fit.
`deletion_filter` in `cipt/diagnose.py`
def deletion_filter(built: Built, keep: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> list[str]

items: **Contract.** Returns, sorted, the names of an irreducible set of rows that cannot all hold: relax each row in name order, keep it relaxed while the model stays infeasible, restore it when relaxing it makes the model feasible. Rows named in keep are never relaxed.
**Modeling idea.** The deletion filter: the rows you cannot relax without the clash disappearing form a conflict, and dropping any one of them gives a plan.
**Taught in** [9.1.3 IIS With MathOpt, gurobipy and Pyomo](../../../../09-diagnostics-and-explainability/37-infeasibility/units/unit-03/9.1.3-iis-with-mathopt-gurobipy-and-pyomo.unit.html).

blocks.text: `feasible` in `cipt/diagnose.py`
def feasible(built: Built) -> bool

items: **Contract.** True unless HiGHS reports the model infeasible: only the termination INFEASIBLE counts as no plan, and INFEASIBLE_OR_UNBOUNDED counts as feasible (every variable is binary, so the model is never unbounded).
**Modeling idea.** The filter only asks one question of each solve: does a plan exist?

**Taught in** [9.1.1 Infeasible, Unbounded, or the Solver Can't Tell](../../../../09-diagnostics-and-explainability/37-infeasibility/units/unit-01/9.1.1-infeasible-unbounded-or-the-solver-cant-tell.unit.html).

blocks.text: `describe` in `cipt/diagnose.py`
def describe(request: Request, name: str) -> str

items: **Contract.** Returns one row in the planners' words, read from its name: `spend in <y> within $<b>k`, `<id> is a must-do`, `<id> is forced in`, `at most one of <ids>` (the group's members in id order, joined by a comma and a space), `<a> and <b> are funded together or not at all`, `<child> started by <t> needs <parent> started by <t - lag>`, `remove at least $<floor>k of risk` (one decimal, thousands commas) for the risk floor; the name itself for any other row. The kind is the part of the name before its first underscore.
**Modeling idea.** A conflict is only useful in the names people can change.
**Taught in** [9.1.6 Turning an IIS Into a Planner Message](../../../../09-diagnostics-and-explainability/37-infeasibility/units/unit-06/9.1.6-turning-an-iis-into-a-planner-message.unit.html).

blocks.text: `explain` in `cipt/diagnose.py`
def explain(request: Request, rows: list[str]) -> Conflict

items: **Contract.** Returns a Conflict with the rows and a message: `No plan meets these <n> rules together; drop or change any one of them:` then one line `  <row>: <description>` per row.
**Modeling idea.** Turn the IIS into a message that says what to change.
**Taught in** [9.1.6 Turning an IIS Into a Planner Message](../../../../09-diagnostics-and-explainability/37-infeasibility/units/unit-06/9.1.6-turning-an-iis-into-a-planner-message.unit.html).

blocks.text: `why_infeasible` in `cipt/diagnose.py`
def why_infeasible(request: Request) -> Conflict | None

items: **Contract.** None when the request has a plan; otherwise the Conflict of the rows that clash.
**Modeling idea.** Run the filter only when the model is infeasible.
**Taught in** [9.1.3 IIS With MathOpt, gurobipy and Pyomo](../../../../09-diagnostics-and-explainability/37-infeasibility/units/unit-03/9.1.3-iis-with-mathopt-gurobipy-and-pyomo.unit.html).

blocks.text: `why_deferred` in `cipt/diagnose.py`
def why_deferred(request: Request, plan, project_id: str) -> Deferral

items: **Contract.** Forces the project in with a row `force_<id>`. When that is feasible, returns the NPV the plan gives up and the funded projects it drops; when it is not, the Conflict of the rows that block it, the force row kept.
**Modeling idea.** Forcing a decision in and re-solving prices it; when no plan exists, the conflict says why.

**Taught in** [9.3.2 Why Selected, Why Deferred: Forcing In and Out](../../../../09-diagnostics-and-explainability/39-explaining-decisions/units/unit-02/9.3.2-why-selected-why-deferred-forcing-in-and-out.unit.html).

blocks.text: `main` in `cipt/__main__.py`
def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int

items: **Contract.** Prints the report; for an infeasible request also prints the conflict message and returns 1. With --why PROJECT for a project the plan leaves out, prints `<id> cannot be funded. <message>` or `Funding <id> costs $<cost>k of NPV and drops <ids or nothing>.` (cost in whole $k, ids joined by a comma and a space); for a project the plan funds, nothing more.
**Modeling idea.** The command line is where the planners read the diagnostics.

**Taught in** [14.2.6 Why It Failed, Why It Was Deferred: A Diagnostics Layer](../../../../14-growing-real-projects/55-project-cipt-planner/units/unit-06/14.2.6-why-it-failed-why-it-was-deferred-a-diagnostics-layer.unit.html).

File: cipt/__init__.py

"""CIPT planner: which capital projects to fund, grown one planner request at a time.

The data it ships with (data/demo.json) is GridCap, a fictional utility invented for this course.
"""
File: cipt/__main__.py

"""python -m cipt EXPORT.json [--why PROJECT]: plan the export and print the report."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse

from .data import read_request
from .diagnose import why_deferred, why_infeasible
from .report import render
from .solve import solve


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="cipt", description="Plan a capital portfolio.")
    parser.add_argument("export", help="the planning export, a JSON file")
    parser.add_argument("--why", metavar="PROJECT", help="explain why PROJECT was not funded")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    request = read_request(args.export)
    plan = solve(request)
    print(render(request, plan))
    if plan.status == "infeasible":
        print(why_infeasible(request).message)
        return 1
    if args.why and args.why not in plan.starts:
        d = why_deferred(request, plan, args.why)
        if d.conflict:
            print(f"{args.why} cannot be funded. {d.conflict.message}")
        else:
            print(f"Funding {args.why} costs ${d.npv_cost:,.0f}k of NPV and drops {', '.join(d.displaced) or 'nothing'}.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""Two goals at once: the trade between NPV and the risk a plan removes.

`frontier` finds plans none of which beats another on both goals, by the epsilon-constraint
method (lesson 8.3.1): maximize NPV while the risk removed must reach a floor, for floors spread
between the two single-goal plans. Each point is finished by a second, lexicographic solve
(lesson 8.2.1) that keeps its NPV and takes as much risk as that NPV allows, so no point is beaten
on one goal by a plan equal on the other (lesson 8.3.2).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from .data import Request
from .model import build
from .plan import Plan
from .solve import solve_built

#: Slack on a goal a second pass must keep: NPV is whole $k; risk is a float sum.
KEEP = {"npv": 0.5, "risk": 1e-6}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Point:
    npv: float
    risk: float
    plan: Plan


def best(request: Request, first: str, floor: float | None = None) -> Plan:
    """Maximize `first`, then the other goal with `first` held at its best (two solves)."""
    built = build(request)
    goal = {"npv": built.npv, "risk": built.risk}
    if floor is not None:
        built.add("risk_floor", built.risk >= floor)
    built.model.maximize(goal[first])
    plan = solve_built(built)
    if plan.status != "optimal":
        return plan
    other = "risk" if first == "npv" else "npv"
    built.add(f"keep_{first}", goal[first] >= getattr(plan, first) - KEEP[first])
    built.model.maximize(goal[other])
    return solve_built(built)


def dominates(a: Point, b: Point) -> bool:
    return a.npv >= b.npv - KEEP["npv"] and a.risk >= b.risk - KEEP["risk"] and \
        (a.npv > b.npv + KEEP["npv"] or a.risk > b.risk + KEEP["risk"])


def frontier(request: Request, points: int = 5) -> list[Point]:
    """Up to `points` non-dominated plans, from the best NPV to the most risk removed."""
    ends = [best(request, "npv"), best(request, "risk")]
    if any(p.status != "optimal" for p in ends):
        return []
    low, high = ends[0].risk, ends[1].risk
    plans = [ends[0]]
    for k in range(1, points - 1):
        plans.append(best(request, "npv", floor=low + k * (high - low) / (points - 1)))
    plans.append(ends[1])
    found: list[Point] = []
    for plan in plans:
        point = Point(plan.npv, plan.risk, plan)
        if plan.status == "optimal" and not any(abs(point.npv - q.npv) <= KEEP["npv"] for q in found):
            found.append(point)
    return [p for p in found if not any(dominates(q, p) for q in found)]

"""A plan: what the solve decided, in the planners' terms."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Plan:
    """The answer to a request.

    `status` is "optimal", "infeasible" or another solver outcome in lower case; `starts` maps each
    funded project to the year its work starts; `objective` is what the model maximized; `npv` and
    `risk` are the plan's NPV and the risk it removes, both in $k, whichever was maximized.
    """

    status: str
    starts: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
    objective: float = 0.0
    npv: float = 0.0
    risk: float = 0.0

    @property
    def funded(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        return tuple(sorted(self.starts))

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from .data import Request
from .plan import Plan


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Scenario:
    name: str
    budget: dict[int, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
    force_in: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    force_out: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    fix_start: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
    note: str = ""


def apply(request: Request, scenario: Scenario) -> Request:
    """The request with the scenario's budgets and overrides. Stub: the request unchanged."""
    return request


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Diff:
    selected: tuple[str, ...]
    deferred: tuple[str, ...]
    shifted: tuple[tuple[str, int, int], ...]


def diff(base: Plan, other: Plan) -> Diff:
    """What changed between two plans. Stub: nothing."""
    return Diff((), (), ())

"""Run: plan the demo export, print the planners' report, why P003 was deferred, and the trade
between NPV and risk.

data/demo.json is GridCap tiny, a fictional utility's portfolio. Its path is taken from this
file's folder, never from the working directory, so the report is the same wherever Run starts.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from cipt.__main__ import main
from cipt.data import read_request
from cipt.goals import frontier

DEMO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "data" / "demo.json"


def show_frontier() -> None:
    """One line per plan on the frontier, from the best NPV to the most risk removed."""
    print()
    print("NPV against risk removed:")
    for point in frontier(read_request(DEMO)):
        print(f"  NPV ${point.npv:,.0f}k  risk removed ${point.risk:,.1f}k  funds {', '.join(point.plan.funded)}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    status = main([str(DEMO), "--why", "P003"])
    show_frontier()
    raise SystemExit(status)
